_about: Plain descriptions of the tables in datasets/open/, for the Data page and one page per table. group orders them. cols explains the columns a reader would not guess.

theory_scorecard_totals.csv.title: How each theory scores
theory_scorecard_totals.csv.about: One row per theory of consciousness: how many of the hard facts it explains, fits, says nothing about, strains against or contradicts, and a weighted score. Start here.

cols.explains: Facts the theory predicted or derives
cols.compatible: Facts it fits, but did not predict
cols.strained: Facts it can only fit with extra assumptions
cols.weighted_score: Points, with better-established facts weighted more
cols.cells_with_proponent_source: Marks backed by something the theory's own authors wrote
cols.name: Full name
cols.weighted_explains: Weighted points from facts it explains

constraint_ledger.csv.title: The facts any theory must explain
constraint_ledger.csv.about: 59 findings about consciousness (blindsight, dreaming, anaesthesia and more), each with an evidence grade and its sources. Every theory is marked against this list.

cols.evidence_grade: A = replicated and robust, B = good but limited, C = suggestive

theory_scorecard.csv.title: Every theory against every fact
theory_scorecard.csv.about: The full grid behind the scores: each theory against each fact, with its mark, where the mark comes from and why.

cols.mark: explains, compatible, silent, strained or contradicts
cols.proponent_position: What the theory's own authors have said, with the source

theory_scorecard_gaps.csv.title: Facts no theory explains
theory_scorecard_gaps.csv.about: The 16 facts that no current theory predicts. Any new theory, ours included, should be judged first on these.

cols.kind: none explains, or every theory strains
cols.compatible: Theories that at least fit it

blind_scoring_marks.csv.title: A second, blind round of marks
blind_scoring_marks.csv.about: The theory-against-fact marks done again by a marker who could not see the first round, to check how much the scores depend on who marks them.

cols.weight: Points for the fact's evidence grade (A = 3, B = 2, C = 1)
cols.in_totals: 1 if the fact counts in the totals

our_theory_coverage.csv.title: Our own theory, marked the same way
our_theory_coverage.csv.about: Two drafts of our candidate theory (T1 and T2) marked against every fact, with a flag wherever the fit was worked out after seeing the fact.

cols.T1_post_hoc: 1 if the fit was found after the fact rather than predicted

theory_tests_scoreboard.csv.title: Theory predictions we tested on brain data
theory_tests_scoreboard.csv.about: Predictions from the theories, written down and sealed before we looked, then tested on open sleep and anaesthesia recordings. Each row says whether the prediction passed.

cols.statistic: The measured result (AUC: 0.5 is chance, 1 is perfect)
cols.verdict: Passed or failed, with the size of effect the test could have caught
cols.prereg_hash: Fingerprint of the sealed plan, published before the result

theory_tests_results.json.title: Full numbers for those tests
theory_tests_results.json.about: Everything behind the theory-test scoreboard: per-dataset results, confidence intervals, permutation tests and the planted-answer checks.

bench_ledger.csv.title: Every test we have run
bench_ledger.csv.about: One row per test from every experiment, passes and failures alike, with its statistic, sample size and how it was corrected for running many tests.

cols.experiment: Which experiment folder it came from
cols.split: Which part of the data it used (held-out or not)
cols.family_size: How many tests share its correction
cols.replicated_independently: Whether a second dataset or lab agreed

lz_slope_results.json.title: Does brain-signal complexity add anything?
lz_slope_results.json.about: A popular complexity measure (LZ) tested against the simpler slope of the brain-signal spectrum across three datasets: how well each tells waking from deep sleep, and whether complexity adds anything once the slope is known.

t1_dream_features.csv.title: Brain signals just before each dream report
t1_dream_features.csv.about: For each awakening in the Tononi serial-awakening study: brain-signal power in several bands just before waking, and whether the person then reported a dream.

cols.label: E = experience reported, NE = no experience, WR = experience without recall
cols.delta5: Slow-wave (1-4 Hz) power in the last 5 s
cols.exp10: Slope of the spectrum over the last 10 s

t1_dream_subject_counts.csv.title: Dream reports per person
t1_dream_subject_counts.csv.about: How many awakenings per person ended in a dream report, no experience, or experience without recall, in the data as analysed.

ground_truth_labels.csv.title: Every open recording, and what we know about the person's state
ground_truth_labels.csv.about: 3,679 recordings or awakenings from open datasets, each labelled with how we know whether the person was conscious: they responded, they reported a dream, or only the drug dose is known.

cols.family: sleep, anaesthesia or disorders of consciousness
cols.behaviour: What the person did (for example a sedation score)
cols.report: What they said on waking, if asked
cols.truth: Kind of evidence: report, behaviour, or none

ground_truth_counts.json.title: Counts behind the data figures
ground_truth_counts.json.about: The totals behind the charts on the Data and Findings pages: recordings by dataset and kind of evidence, and dream reports by sleep stage and lab.

dream_sets.csv.title: The 20 dream studies in the DREAM database
dream_sets.csv.about: Each study pooled in DREAM: how many awakenings and people, how many dream reports, recording quality, size and licence.

dream_access.csv.title: Which dream studies we could actually download
dream_access.csv.about: For each DREAM study: whether the download worked when we checked, its licence and size, and the dream / no-dream counts by sleep stage.

cols.access_live: Whether the download worked when we checked
cols.N2_exp: Dream reports from stage N2 sleep (N3 = deep sleep, REM = rapid eye movement)
